chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in a man entering iḥrām in a dyed, striped garment.

key_terms.ثَوْبٍ: a garment or piece of clothing
key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: to enter the state of iḥrām for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.ٱلرَّجُلُ: a man; the legal subject addressed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to enter iḥrām wearing a dyed or striped garment?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning what may be worn in the state of iḥrām. It indicates that entering iḥrām in a dyed or striped garment is permissible and not objectionable.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2600 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"There is no harm if a man enters Ihram wearing a dyed or striped garment."
